title: This School Year, Try the Minimalist Approach to Student Motivation
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Stuart revisits his own 10-strategy Will to Learn framework and asks which strategies could be cut without losing critical impact, aiming for a more sustainable minimalist starting point for teachers overwhelmed by the full list. Working strategy by strategy, he eliminates Improve at One Thing, Gentle Urgency, and Feast of Knowledge, not because they're unimportant, but because their effects are substantially covered by the remaining seven, or because removing them forces the very focus they were meant to create. He lands on seven core strategies, MGCs, Mini-Sermons, Valued Within, Woodenization, Define Success, Unpack Outcomes, and Normalize Struggle, and shows how the latter three form an interlocking trio addressing the Effort-Efficacy Flywheel. The piece is a practical decision document for teachers deciding where to start each fall.
points: Stuart argues that removing Improve at One Thing is itself an act of following its own advice, since a smaller list of strategies naturally forces the focus that strategy was meant to instill.
Woodenization, Define Success, and Unpack Outcomes are grouped as an interconnected trio that intervenes at the three breakage points of the Effort-Efficacy Flywheel.

Cutting Feast of Knowledge is framed as the hardest trade-off, since knowledge-building took Stuart years of practice, thinking, and tinkering to implement well, too heavy a lift for a minimalist starting point.
He keeps Mini-Sermons as one of the highest-leverage strategies because it enhances both Credibility and Value with as little effort as possible.
quotes: What I've found is that even the short list of 10 strategies I write about can be pretty overwhelming. It's too much to focus on at any given time.
Improve at One Thing – This can go because, by getting rid of it, we'll actually be doing it. By giving ourselves fewer strategies to focus on, we can get better at each one faster.
But the reason I didn't is because, by removing the three that I did, you get efficiency and focus gains that exceed the simple three strategy reduction.

Mini-sermons are simple, brief, repeated attempts to creatively and confidently explain to your students why they're doing the work they're doing. These enhance Credibility and Value with as little effort as possible.
So, I went from 10 to 7. Not much of a reduction, right? It seemed like that to me at first. I was frustrated.
So this school year, my recommendation is to play with just these seven tools as you seek to do something productive about student motivation problems in your setting.
